rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct-match outcome is supported. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA publication (Million Veteran Program AAA genetics paper), reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, moderate discriminative signal) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and has endpoint fidelity (prevalent AAA) without risk-wrapper packaging; several other candidates report only full-model discrimination or weakly comparable metrics. Runners-up: PGS003973 is from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis paper and reports a high C-index (0.882) with basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex), but the metric appears to be full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), limiting comparability. PGS001784 reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.014661) and is genome-wide (PRS-CS-auto) with large EUR evaluation, but it is from a broad framework/portability-style paper (“Global Biobank analyses...”), which domain guidance penalizes versus disease-focused models when endpoint/metric evidence is otherwise similar. Overall confidence is moderate because most candidates lack clearly PRS-only AUROC and several reported AUROC/C-index values are likely full-model and thus not directly comparable for PRS ranking.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target concept via alcohol dependence/AUD alignment (PGS002738/PGS002739 have trait_efo="alcohol dependence" and phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201/PGS000202 map to "alcohol dependence measurement" with DSM-5 AUD criteria count). PGS002738 is best supported because it has the most directly aligned disease label (AUD/alcohol dependence), a clear discriminative effect-size style metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) and a reasonably large EUR evaluation sample (n=7,900). Main limitation: covariates are unknown and there is no PRS-only AUC/R2, so comparability and standalone PRS strength cannot be fully assessed. Runner-up PGS002739 is also directly aligned (AUD/alcohol dependence) and reports OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76 (1.32–2.34), but it is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples (AFR 100%), making it less generally supported in this context than the EUR-evaluated PGS002738. Third-ranked PGS000201 remains a direct match through DSM-5 AUD criteria count and has the strongest incremental ΔR² among the two UKB siblings (0.01192 vs 0.00456 for PGS000202) with a larger validation sample (n=7,599 vs n=1,251), but its trait_reported is broader (problematic alcohol use) and the reported effect size (β=0.099) is less directly interpretable than the OR evidence in PGS002738.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned reported phenotypes. PGS004913 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported explicitly matches alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis) and is disease-focused (heavy drinkers; dedicated cirrhosis PRS paper), with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and supportive effect-size evidence (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4). However, its reported performance is limited to an R²=0.029 (not explicitly stated as PRS-only vs full-model) and lacks AUROC/C-index, so overall evidence remains incomplete.

Runner-up PGS000704 has strong structural properties (very large variant count; snpnet multi-PRS) and large evaluation size, with basic covariates; but its only visible discrimination is a full-model C-index/AUROC-like metric (0.711) plus modest HR per SD (1.18), and the publication context appears biomarker/pan-trait oriented rather than cirrhosis-focused, making the full-model metric less directly interpretable as PRS strength.

Runner-up PGS001777 is clearly disease-focused and directly labeled alcohol-related cirrhosis, with a strong top-vs-bottom OR (6.18), but it is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and has a small validation sample (n=1,390), which together reduce confidence in robustness despite the direct match.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported explicitly angina/I20/PheCode 411.3). Best-supported is PGS001262 because it has strong endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed angina), reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.58683; PGS R2=0.01304) plus incremental AUROC (0.0098), and uses only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), making the performance evidence more interpretable than models that report only full-model metrics or only ORs. Runner-up PGS001261 is very similar (same study family/covariates/PRS-only metrics) with slightly lower PRS-only performance but comparable evidence quality; it is time-to-event, which is a mild endpoint-type penalty for a generic disease target. Second runner-up PGS005048 has good endpoint fidelity (PheCode angina) and a strong reported OR (1.487) with a high full-model C-index (0.7669), but lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and comes from a method-comparison context with multiple near-clone siblings, making cross-model comparability and selection less certain. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the pool contains multiple near-equivalent direct matches and several candidates rely on non-PRS-only metrics (full-model C-index/AUROC or OR-only), limiting a clearly unambiguous best choice from the visible evidence.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. The pool splits into (i) UKB framework/portability-derived scores (PGS001267/PGS001268 from the pan-trait sparse UKB paper; PGS001876/PGS002089 from the UKB portability benchmarking paper) and (ii) a Taiwanese EAS-only study family (PGS003420–PGS003424) reporting only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates.

Best pick: PGS002089 is preferred because it is endpoint-faithful (phenotyping_reported: Ankylosing spondylitis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a much larger variant set (22,026) than the sparse snpnet models (10 variants), and it provides a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0919 with CI) in European validation. This combination offers more directly comparable PRS evidence than the EAS-only models that report only full-model AUROC.

Runners-up: PGS001267 and PGS001268 both provide explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 (and incremental/full-model metrics with basic covariates) and are phenotype-aligned; however, they come from the "across 813 traits" sparse framework paper and are extremely sparse (10 variants), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk. Between them, the time-to-event framing in PGS001268 is a mild endpoint penalty for generic disease-risk use, so PGS001267 is ranked slightly ahead.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: there is no clearly disease-focused multi-cohort AS PRS here; most options are framework/benchmarking-derived, and key metrics are missing or non-comparable for several candidates (e.g., EAS-only models with only full-model AUROC and unknown covariates; portability models lacking AUROC/R2). This leaves meaningful residual uncertainty despite a reasonable preference for PGS002089.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo both aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), a disease-focused Nat Genet study context, and it reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). The main limitation is that the reported C-index is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (multiple cardiometabolic comorbidities and BMI/smoking/renal failure), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates. Runners-up: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis model with incident endpoint and a moderate-to-strong HR (1.64, with CI), but lacks comparable discrimination metrics and has less explicit development-cohort detail. Between the remaining two measurement-labeled siblings (PGS005255 mean pressure gradient; PGS005256 peak aortic velocity), both still use incident aortic stenosis phenotyping but are less directly aligned at the trait label level; PGS005255 is selected as the second runner-up based on essentially identical visible evidence to PGS005256 (same method/variant count/HR magnitude) with no clear differentiator, so confidence remains moderate rather than high.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo=arthritis) and two "Other arthritis" models (PGS004477, PGS004547; trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the strongest direct match on endpoint fidelity because its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly arthritis (nos), and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC, enabling interpretation of PRS contribution (and remaining below the provided heritability ceiling guidance). However, it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as systematically underperforming disease-focused models and thus lowers confidence/quality despite exact label match. The runners-up (PGS004547, then PGS004477) are also direct-match on trait_efo=arthritis and are not from the 813-traits framework, but they provide only limited effect-size evidence (OR only) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics, making them less well-supported overall than PGS001135 while still plausible alternatives given the framework penalty on PGS001135.

Direct-match candidates for asthma are abundant (66). The best-supported direct-match choice from the visible list is PGS002727 because it has strong endpoint fidelity for a major clinically relevant subtype (“Pediatric asthma”), very large validation sample size (n=391,820), and—critically—reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) alongside AUROC=0.66 and R²=0.04, providing more PRS-comparable evidence than most alternatives that report only full-model metrics or partial correlations. Main limitation: phenotype is pediatric-specific (not generic all-ages asthma) and covariates are listed as “Unknown,” which lowers comparability confidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS001344): strong direct asthma endpoint (“Asthma diagnosed by doctor”) with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.64568; PGS R²(no covariates)=0.05973) and basic covariates, but it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation.

Runner-up 2 (PGS001782): direct asthma endpoint with genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS-auto), multi-biobank training cohorts, and reasonable reported metrics (AUROC=0.659; Nagelkerke R² with covariates regressed out=0.048844), but the evaluation shown is EUR-only and the evidence package is thinner than PGS002727’s (no strong per-SD OR/HR reported). Overall, while there is at least one clearly direct-match candidate, remaining uncertainty about endpoint scope (pediatric vs general asthma) and cross-study comparability prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ selection.

All 6 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=atopic eczema, but endpoint fidelity differs materially. PGS002755 is the best-supported direct match because its phenotyping_reported is a generic, target-aligned endpoint (“Incident atopic dermatitis”) rather than a restricted therapy-induced subtype, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants) with a reported PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS=1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large EUR evaluation (n=337,910). The main limitation is that it does not report PRS-only AUROC/R² (only an HR), so comparative performance vs other direct-match models is not fully resolvable from the visible metadata.

Runners-up: PGS004587 is also endpoint-faithful (“Incident atopic dermatitis”) with a reported HR (1.153, 95% CI 1.037–1.282) but is structurally weaker (23 genome-wide significant SNPs) and appears embedded in an exposure-integration context (air pollution) which can reduce comparability even though the listed covariates are standard. PGS001773 is direct but targets a narrower severity subtype (“Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis”) and reports only full-model metrics (AUROC=0.93; R²=0.49) with covariates; per the provided domain guidance, full-model AUROC/R² are not substitutable for PRS-only metrics and the very high values raise concern that performance is largely covariate-driven or otherwise non-comparable.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter), so ranking is driven by endpoint fidelity plus the most PRS-informative performance evidence while discounting risk-wrapper packaging. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet 2025) with a direct AF endpoint and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus extensive performance record support (record_count=45) and basic covariate set that includes demographics/array plus CHARGE-AF (a risk-calculator term that is a comparability concern, but here it is listed as a covariate rather than the phenotype itself). Runner-up PGS005313 is also a disease-focused AF score (Nat Commun 2025) with direct AF phenotyping, strong reported AUROC (0.78 with tight CI) and strong OR (1.82), with only basic covariates (age, sex), but it has less visible validation/performance breadth (record_count=1) than PGS005168. Third, PGS002814 (Nat Genet 2023) is a very large cross-ancestry AF GWAS-derived score with direct AF endpoint and supportive metrics (AUROC 0.74; pseudo-R2 0.14) in East Asian evaluation; it is strong but less directly comparable if the intended deployment is not East Asian, and it has only one visible performance record. Confidence is Moderate because many other direct-match candidates exist with heterogeneous endpoints (incident-only, time-to-event, AF/flutter composites) and many report only full-model metrics, making cross-model comparability imperfect. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct-match in the sense that their trait fields include atrial flutter (PGS001263 is exact: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Atrial flutter”; the other three are “Atrial fibrillation and flutter”, which still explicitly contains atrial flutter). PGS001263 is preferred because it has the strongest endpoint fidelity to the target (atrial flutter specifically) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.61716; PGS-only R2=0.02517) with only basic covariates; its PGS-only R2 is also below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so it passes the sanity-check. However, confidence is limited because PGS001263 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly, and because the strongest competing models (PGS002050/PGS001841) are from a different framework family (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores”) and do not report PRS-only AUROC/R2 here (only partial-r), making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete. Among the runners-up, PGS002050 is ranked above PGS001841 because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (554,908 vs 3,980) while sharing the same endpoint label and study context, which is supportive when other evidence is otherwise similar and metrics are sparse.

Both visible candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to autism spectrum disorder, but PGS000327 has substantially better endpoint fidelity: its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder,” whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn),” creating an explicit phenotype mismatch despite the trait_reported/EFO label. PGS000327 also shows stronger visible performance evidence (full_model_r2=0.0245 and OR=1.33 per SD) than PGS002790 (partial R²=0.00546; no effect sizes shown), and it is from an ASD-focused Nat Genet study with clear multi-cohort development. Confidence is Moderate (not High) because neither model reports clearly PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS-only R²/AUROC), and PGS002790 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (SDPR) with many variants, which is structurally favorable but not enough here to outweigh the explicit phenotype mismatch and weaker reported metric.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (basal cell carcinoma) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint fidelity (most have phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma; two newer models note phenotyping_reported = Keratinocyte cancers; one is restricted to childhood cancer survivors).

Best pick: PGS000452 is best supported on the visible evidence because it combines strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma; basic covariates: age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest reported discrimination/effect evidence among the PRSweb/Cancer PRSweb cluster: full-model AUROC 0.632 (CI 0.616–0.647) and a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (CI 1.57–1.761), plus a strong top-1% vs rest OR 3.61. While AUROC is full-model (not PRS-only), covariates are basic, making it more comparable than covariate-heavy packages.

Runners-up: PGS000454 is essentially a near-clone with the same AUROC (0.632, same CI) and very similar per-SD OR (1.661) and covariates/endpoint, leaving it as the closest alternative. PGS000456 is next-best within the same coherent Cancer PRSweb family with very similar endpoint/covariates and nearly identical performance (AUROC 0.63; per-SD OR 1.633) and strong top-1% vs rest OR (3.95).

Main limitation lowering confidence: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2; most reported AUROCs are full-model and thus not strictly comparable as standalone PRS metrics. Several models are extremely close in performance within the same study family, making the top choice only moderately separable based on the visible metadata. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/trait_reported. PGS001824 is preferred because it has the most endpoint-faithful labeling/phenotyping for the target (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both specifically "Disorders of bilirubin excretion" with trait_efo exactly "bilirubin metabolism disease"), and it provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (partial correlation 0.0716 in European validation). PGS002032 is a very close runner-up with the same endpoint and essentially identical reported partial-r, but with a more genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) and far higher variant count; however, the visible evidence does not include PRS-only AUC/R² for either portability score, so the two are hard to separate decisively from the provided metadata alone. PGS000924 reports strong-looking discrimination metrics including PGS-only AUROC and R², but it comes from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet with only 5 variants) and uses a time-to-event composite phenotype (porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism), which lowers confidence that its high AUROC reflects robust standalone PRS performance for the specific target endpoint. Overall, direct matches exist but the best choice remains limited by missing comparable PRS-only metrics for the two most endpoint-aligned candidates and by framework/time-to-event concerns for the high-AUROC alternative. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to the target trait family (bipolar disorder and bipolar I/II subtypes) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), leaving limited differentiating evidence. Endpoint fidelity is weakened across the set because phenotyping_reported fields are not bipolar diagnosis endpoints (they reference cognition/behavior measures), creating ambiguity about whether the reported validation metrics reflect bipolar disorder prediction versus association with other phenotypes. Given the target is broad ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is preferred for closest trait alignment (bipolar disorder rather than subtype) and slightly higher variant count, but this is a marginal advantage; runners-up are the subtype scores PGS002787 (bipolar I) and PGS002788 (bipolar II), with PGS002788 having slightly higher reported partial R² but still under the same endpoint ambiguity. Overall confidence is low due to the phenotype/endpoint mismatch and lack of PRS-comparable AUC/PRS-only R².

All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but they differ in endpoint specificity and evidence quality. PGS002034 and PGS001826 both target a specific coagulation-disorder diagnosis (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”; phenotyping_reported matches), which is a cleaner disease endpoint than the time-to-event “other coagulation defects” framing in PGS001033 (domain guidance flags time-to-event as a warning signal when alternatives exist). Between the two congenital-deficiency siblings from the same publication/cohort/covariate context, PGS002034 is structurally stronger (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants) while having essentially identical reported partial correlation (0.0563 vs 0.0562), so it is the best-supported pick on the visible evidence. PGS001826 is the closest runner-up due to near-identical endpoint and performance evidence but weaker structural properties. PGS001033 is ranked third despite having explicit AUROC fields because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely sparse 1-variant model and a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are negative signals per the provided domain knowledge. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the best candidate is for a specific congenital coagulation-factor deficiency rather than the broad umbrella “blood coagulation disease,” and key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for the top two candidates, limiting certainty. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for breast carcinoma (multiple models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma / phenotyping_reported=breast cancer). Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Breast cancer), no covariate leakage (covariates=0), and is a multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) with the strongest reported discrimination in this coherent disease-endpoint benchmarking family (full_model_auc=0.6625; R²=0.0764; OR=1.83) evaluated in a European validation set (n=48,968). The two strongest runners-up from the same high-support cluster are PGS004040 and PGS004025 (both LDpred2 variants with very similar AUROC ~0.6598 and R² ~0.0736–0.0739, same endpoint/covariate setting and validation context). Main limitation: metrics across the broader candidate list are often full-model AUROC (not PRS-only), and several other direct-match models exist with different study designs and covariates; thus, while PGS004153 is the best-supported within the visible evidence, cross-study comparability remains imperfect, keeping confidence at Moderate.

All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo and largely consistent phenotyping_reported. PGS000316 is best supported because it targets a straightforward coeliac disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is from a disease-focused clinical-care context, and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.879 with CI) with very large validation sample size (n=379,767), making it the most substantiated direct-match package in the visible set. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from the provided metadata, lowering certainty. Runner-up PGS000040 is also disease-focused with the highest reported AUROC (0.9) but likewise only as full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and a much smaller validation sample (n=2,476). Runner-up PGS001301 provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.82867; PGS R2 0.14224) and basic covariates, but comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as typically less reliable than disease-focused models when such alternatives exist. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported overall because it comes from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis/risk-stratification study and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555), which is a positive structural signal versus sparse/GWAS-hit scores when endpoint alignment is comparable. Its evaluation is European with a reported C-index (0.613) and HR per SD (1.33), providing at least moderate effect-size evidence.

However, the choice is not high-confidence because the available performance evidence is mostly full-model discrimination (C-index/AUROC) rather than clearly PRS-only metrics, and PGS003428’s reported discrimination is not clearly superior to other direct-match options; additionally, some alternatives have larger apparent full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000073/PGS000784 ~0.745) but those are discounted because they are full-model metrics with multiple non-genetic covariates and come from cross-cancer/pan-cancer integration contexts.

Runners-up: PGS000073 is the strongest remaining EUR direct-match with coherent incident cervical cancer endpoint and moderate HR (1.22) plus large evaluation sample (n=211,795), albeit based on only 10 genome-wide significant variants and cross-cancer evaluation framing. PGS005165 is the best-supported non-EUR direct-match (EAS GWAS/EVAL) with an incident cervical cancer endpoint and HR 1.2 in a large Chinese cohort (n=57,359), but it is limited by small variant count (15) and ancestry specificity relative to the predominantly EUR-evaluated set.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or the closely related composite “cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”). PGS001174 is best supported because it is the only model in the list with explicit PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS-only R2=0.028; incremental AUROC=0.043; European validation), and its PGS-only R2 is plausible relative to the provided local heritability ceiling context (h2_obs≈0.021; liability h2≈0.137). The main limitation is that PGS001174 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused scores; however, the other direct-match candidates largely lack comparable AUC/R2 and therefore cannot be more strongly supported from the visible evidence alone.

Runners-up: PGS002072 and PGS001861 (same publication family; same endpoint ‘cholelithiasis and cholecystitis’; same training/validation context) have partial-r estimates (0.098 vs 0.0948) providing some quantitative support, but still lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and are from a portability framework study, so they remain less well-supported than PGS001174 given the available metadata.

All listed candidates are direct matches to chronic kidney disease via trait_efo/trait_reported, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable the reported performance is as PRS-specific. PGS002237 is best supported because it is from a CKD-focused study explicitly aiming to predict CKD across ancestries (Nat Med 2022), uses a clear clinical CKD definition (stage 3+; eGFR <45), has multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.47) alongside a high AUROC (0.78) in the selected European validation record (noting AUROC is full-model and includes multiple clinical covariates, so it is discounted but still supportive). The two strongest runners-up are PGS005090 (AFR-focused CKD stage 3+ with very strong reported full-model AUROC 0.9 and R2 0.1 plus OR 1.41 in African American/Afro-Caribbean evaluation; strong but ancestry-specific and metrics may be covariate-influenced) and PGS005113 (CKDGen-based PRS-CS with a solid OR 1.35 and large validation n=48,603, with relatively basic covariates, but lacking PRS-only metrics/AUROC and less explicit CKD stage definition than PGS002237). Confidence is Moderate because most candidates lack PRS-only metrics, several reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable across differing covariate sets, and there is a large near-clone family (PGS003988–PGS004158) with similar endpoints but lower AUROC (~0.59) and smaller development sample, making ranking beyond the top choice somewhat evidence-limited.

All 10 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, with varying endpoint fidelity (e.g., COPD, chronic airway obstruction, ICD J44, time-to-event, algorithmic COPD, and emphysema). The best-supported direct-match is PGS001783 because it targets COPD with phenotype-aligned labeling, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus an AUROC value (0.74, though not explicitly PGS-only). Its PRS R2 is consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling guidance (h2_liability ~0.0388), supporting metric plausibility. Runner-up PGS001788 is the closest sibling (same paper/method/endpoint family) but has materially weaker PRS-comparable R2 (0.0163). Among the remaining candidates, PGS001332 is the strongest of the snpnet COPD-labeled models on endpoint alignment (explicit COPD; not time-to-event or algorithmic-only) and has explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.53971; PGS-only R2 0.00235), though it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and shows weak PRS-only signal. Confidence is Moderate because several candidates have endpoint variations (J44 vs COPD vs chronic airway obstruction) and some newer J44 models report only effect sizes (OR) with unknown covariates, limiting comparability, while the chosen PRS-CS models lack explicit PGS-only AUROC and have relatively small/variable validation sample sizes.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (cirrhosis of liver), but they vary in endpoint specificity (generic cirrhosis vs alcohol-related subtypes) and in how PRS-comparable the reported metrics are. PGS004621 is best supported because it is an exact trait_efo match (cirrhosis of liver) with phenotype reported as “Cirrhosis”, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and comes from a disease-focused Nat Genet cirrhosis genetics study with a very large validation sample (n=1,153,995). Its reported AUROC (0.68) is a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), but covariates are basic (age, sex, PCs), making it more comparable than models with unclear packaging; it also reports an OR per SD of 1.42 (moderate effect-size support).

Runner-up PGS000726 is also an exact trait_efo match with phenotype “Cirrhosis” and a large multi-cohort training set; it reports an OR per SD of 1.32 and a strong tail contrast (OR 2.26 top 20% vs bottom 20%), but it is a sparse 12-variant GWS score and lacks AUROC/R2, leaving less structural support than PGS004621. Runner-up PGS000704 is a close direct match but is explicitly alcoholic cirrhosis (subtype mismatch vs generic cirrhosis) and its reported C-index 0.711 is a full-model metric (age/sex/PCs/batch) without PRS-only metrics; effect size HR 1.18 suggests weaker PRS signal. Confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2, and several are subtype-restricted (alcohol-related) or have phenotype-field inconsistencies (e.g., PGS000776 labeled cirrhosis but described as incident cirrhosis in NAFLD at-risk individuals).

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the target EFO term and with identical reported/phenotyped endpoint text (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), same publication family (UKB portability paper), same training cohort (UKB), similar evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), same validation sample size, and essentially identical reported partial correlation (0.0563 vs 0.0562). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes available to separate them, selection falls back to structural signals: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (32,552 vs 45) and has a trivially higher partial-r, making it the slightly better-supported choice. However, because both models come from a portability/framework context and the performance evidence is limited to partial-r with near-identical estimates, the direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both report/phenotype “Corneal dystrophy” with matching EFO), from the same UKB portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size, so endpoint fidelity is equally strong but the overall evidence base is limited to this framework-style context and lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2. Between them, PGS002042 is modestly better supported by the only comparable performance signal shown (higher partial correlation 0.0471 vs 0.0384 in the selected European validation record) and by a more genome-wide shrinkage-style method/structure (LDpred2 with 59,944 variants vs penalized regression sparse 38 variants), which is a supportive structural differentiator when endpoints and study context are otherwise near-identical. Confidence is not high because both models come from the same portability framework paper and neither provides PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect-size summaries here, making the performance comparison narrow and potentially sensitive to reporting/record-selection details.

All ranked models are direct matches to the target trait (coronary artery disease) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS003725 is best supported because it is a disease-focused CAD score with strong reported per-SD effect sizes (HR=1.75; OR=2.14) and a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with substantial variant count (1,296,172), plus large-scale evaluation (n=308,264) and multi-ancestry evaluation context, which jointly supports robustness beyond a single-cohort setting. The top runners-up are PGS003726 (same publication family, same endpoint, similar method/variant count, strong HR=1.73 but less extensive effect-size reporting than PGS003725) and PGS002244 (direct CAD endpoint, LDpred genome-wide score with large evaluation n=343,676 and strong OR=1.64). Main limitation: across many candidates, most reported discrimination metrics are full-model AUROC/C-index (often with unknown or potentially non-comparable covariates) and PRS-only metrics are largely absent, so the ranking relies heavily on endpoint fidelity plus effect-size evidence and structural/method signals; several other direct CAD scores (e.g., PGS000018 with AUROC=0.89 but very small validation n=3,309, and PGS001780 with AUROC=0.913 but unclear covariate comparability) remain meaningful competitors, lowering confidence from High to Moderate.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS004254 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with very large variant count (744,682), and it reports a strong effect size (OR=2.18 per SD, 95% CI 2.05–2.32), which is supportive of meaningful PRS discrimination. However, its reported AUROC=0.72 appears to be a full-model metric (only full_model_auc populated; no PGS-only AUROC/R2), so performance comparability vs the snpnet models is limited, lowering confidence.

Runners-up: PGS001331 and PGS001330 are from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk vs disease-focused scores. Between them, PGS001331 is slightly better supported than PGS001330 due to marginally higher PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R2 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with otherwise similar covariates and validation context; PGS001330 is third and also has a time-to-event phenotype label, which is a mild endpoint-fidelity warning for a generic disease-risk target.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (dementia) are present, including multiple models with trait_efo=dementia and/or phenotyping_reported explicitly referencing incident all-cause dementia. PGS005170 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia), uses an explicitly integrative multi-PRS construction (method indicates aggregation of 24 component PRSs, a positive structural signal per domain knowledge), and reports a directly relevant discrimination metric (AUROC=0.761) plus an HR=1.25 with basic covariates including age/sex/PCs and APOE alleles. The main limitation is that many other dementia/AD-related candidates exist with heterogeneous endpoints (e.g., time-to-event unspecified dementia, AD-specific dementia, vascular dementia) and several report only full-model AUROC or non-PRS-comparable metrics, making cross-candidate performance comparisons imperfect; thus confidence is not High.

Runners-up: PGS000823 is strongly aligned to dementia via phenotyping_reported=incident all-cause dementia and provides a hazard-ratio contrast (top vs bottom tertile HR=1.36), but lacks explicit PRS-only metrics and is AD-labeled rather than dementia-labeled. PGS002249 has phenotyping_reported=incident dementia with a large validation sample (n=196,383) and a strong HR (high vs low genetic risk HR=1.91), but its trait_reported is Alzheimer’s disease (not dementia) and the method/covariate context suggests a broader risk-prediction framing, reducing endpoint/metric comparability versus the best pick.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported aligned to depressive disorder / major depressive disorder). PGS002036 is best supported on visible evidence because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Depression; trait_efo: depressive disorder), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with large variant count (807,338), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0556 with CI) in a consistent UKB portability evaluation context. Runners-up: PGS004760 is also directly aligned (phenotyping_reported: Depression; trait_efo: major depressive disorder) and uses an ensemble-style method (PRSmixPlus) with a reported incremental R2 (0.024), but that metric is full-model incremental (not PRS-only) and validation is smaller (n=9,462). PGS003578 is directly aligned (Major Depressive Disorder (Lifetime)) with modest R2 (0.0257) but comes from a preprint family with multiple near-clone siblings and no PRS-only AUROC/clear PRS-only R2 indicated, limiting comparability. Overall confidence is moderated by heterogeneous metric types across candidates (partial-r vs incremental R2 vs full-model AUROC/C-index/HR) and several candidates having endpoints that are proxies or non-disease outcomes (e.g., antidepressant side effects, brain imaging), making cross-model performance comparison uncertain.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = dilated cardiomyopathy) with endpoint-relevant phenotyping_reported (either clinical dilated cardiomyopathy or non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy). Per provided domain guidance, MTAG-labeled siblings are mildly preferred within the same study family when endpoint remains the same disease.

PGS004951 is best supported because it is an MTAG-enhanced dilated cardiomyopathy PRS with a direct clinical DCM endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy), uses only basic covariates (Sex, PC1-12), and shows the strongest visible effect-size evidence among the clinical-endpoint models (OR 1.93) alongside a reported univariate (PRS-only) AUC of 0.67. 

Runners-up: PGS004949 is also MTAG and shows strong PRS-only AUC (0.68) and strong OR (1.91) but is aligned to a non-ischemic DCM endpoint rather than the more generic clinical DCM endpoint, making it slightly less directly aligned to the broad target label. PGS004862 is an MTAG model with very large European validation (n=347,585) and slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.71) than its non-MTAG sibling, but it lacks explicit PRS-only AUC and uses full-model metrics that are less comparable for PRS ranking.

Main limitation: performance reporting is heterogeneous across candidates (some report PRS-only AUC, others mainly full-model AUROC/R²), and evaluation ancestries differ (some evaluated in MAE-only), which prevents a high-confidence, purely metric-driven separation.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS004614 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused diverticular disease GWAS study (Cell Genom; not a pan-trait framework), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR; ~1.08M variants), and reports the strongest visible discrimination signal in this list (full-model AUROC 0.76 with CI) while using disclosed covariates (family history, age, sex). Main limitation: the only reported AUROC is full-model (no PGS-only AUROC/R² shown), and inclusion of family history is a comparability concern per the provided domain guidance, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly inferred.

Runner-up PGS000997 is a direct-match but is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework ("across 813 traits" snpnet), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores; however it does provide explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only R²=0.01777; PGS-only AUROC=0.591) with basic covariates and a clean ICD10-like endpoint (diverticular disease of intestine, time-to-event). Second runner-up PGS004544 is also a direct-match and has a structurally favorable ensemble/meta-PRS method label (RFDiseasemetaPRS) and a moderate per-SD OR (~1.32), but lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R² and has unknown covariates, making it harder to rank above the metric-supported PGS000997; it edges PGS004474 only by slightly higher reported OR with otherwise similar metadata.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported aligns with Dupuytren’s disease/contracture). PGS002092 is preferred because, within the same publication family and endpoint as PGS001880 (both from the UKB portability paper with identical phenotype/covariates/ancestry evaluation mix), it shows slightly stronger reported PRS-comparable performance (partial-r 0.0797 vs 0.0783, with overlapping CIs) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (484,484 variants), which is a supportive structural signal when endpoints are otherwise identical. PGS001880 is the closest runner-up as the near-clone sibling with nearly identical partial-r but fewer variants and a penalized regression approach. PGS001254 is ranked third despite having explicit AUROC/R² fields because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (a known weaker study archetype for external generalization per the provided domain knowledge) and is extremely sparse (11 variants), even though it reports PGS-only AUROC ~0.665 and PGS-only R² ~0.0247. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the top two candidates lack standard PRS discrimination metrics (AUC/R² are null) and are supported mainly by partial correlation plus structural/method signals, leaving meaningful uncertainty in cross-model comparability.

All 4 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=follicular lymphoma, but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS002304 has the cleanest phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”) and provides the strongest visible discrimination metric among candidates (full-model AUROC=0.61 in EUR eval), making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the provided metadata. However, its covariates are unknown and the AUROC shown is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), limiting comparability and lowering certainty.

Runners-up: PGS000644 and PGS000643 are coherent siblings from the same publication with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and EUR-only development/evaluation; between them, PGS000644 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.538 vs 0.532) and slightly higher pseudo-R² (0.00349 vs 0.00282), so it ranks ahead of PGS000643. PGS003455 is deprioritized despite exact trait_reported because phenotyping_reported is explicitly mismatched (“Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”), creating endpoint incoherence for the target trait.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to the target trait glaucoma (or its dominant subtype POAG) based on trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS004944 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (POAG; self-reported but still explicit), reports a strong PRS effect size (OR=1.74) and a reported AUROC (0.748), and is evaluated in a very large, explicitly multi-ancestry validation sample (n=407,667), which supports robustness/transportability. The main limitation is that the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), so it is not strictly comparable across candidates; thus selection relies heavily on effect size plus study/validation context.

Runners-up: PGS001792 is a direct POAG model using PRS-CS-auto with very large evaluation (n=347,396) and supportive discrimination evidence (AUROC=0.777) plus a PRS-comparable R2 reported as covariates-regressed-out (Nagelkerke R2=0.03209). PGS002761 is a direct glaucoma model using PRS-CS with a strong reported effect size (OR=1.68) and a sizable European validation (n=39,444), but lacks explicit AUROC/R2, lowering comparability. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because multiple strong direct-match candidates exist with partially non-comparable performance reporting (full-model vs PRS-only metrics) and differing endpoint formulations (generic glaucoma vs POAG vs time-to-event), leaving meaningful residual ambiguity. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match gout candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=gout). PGS004160 is best supported because it is a direct gout endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Gout"), uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; domain knowledge: multi-score aggregation is a strong structural positive), has no non-genetic covariates listed (covariates: "0", reducing risk of covariate-driven inflation), and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the clean-covariate gout models in this list (full-model AUROC 0.6936 with relatively high R² 0.0893). Runners-up: PGS004047 (LDpred2.CV) and PGS004018 (lassosum.CV) are also direct gout endpoints with covariates "0" and strong reported AUROC/R² (0.6851/0.0801 and 0.6779/0.0734, respectively), but lack the multi-PRS ensemble advantage and have slightly weaker reported metrics. Confidence is Moderate because most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not explicitly PGS-only), making cross-model performance comparability imperfect; additionally, some other gout candidates have very high full-model AUROC but with heavier/unknown covariates (e.g., PGS000199 includes arthritis outpatient diagnostic context; PGS002307 includes extensive clinical covariates), which are discounted per the provided domain guidance.

All three candidates are direct matches for the target trait (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry set and validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown, which domain guidance cautions against using as a primary discriminator. Given that limitation, PGS005271 is best supported because it shows the strongest PRS-associated effect size (OR per SD ≈ 1.55, meeting the domain ‘strong’ signal guideline) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with ~1.085M variants, while its full-model AUROC is similar to siblings (0.630 vs 0.639 and 0.605; small differences are likely noise). Runner-up PGS005270 has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.639) but is a sparse P+T score with only 55 variants and a very weak OR (~1.04), reducing confidence that the AUROC reflects PRS signal. PGS005272 is another PRSCS genome-wide score but has weaker effect size (OR ~1.42) and lower full-model AUROC (0.605) than PGS005271. Overall confidence is moderate because the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2, incremental metrics, covariates) are missing/unknown across all candidates.

Direct-match candidates are present with clear phenotype alignment to heart failure (multiple models with trait_efo="heart failure" or "congestive heart failure"). Among the visible set, the strongest direct-match support comes from the coherent cluster of CHF PheCode 428.1 models from the same 2024 HGG Adv publication (MVP training; consistent covariates: age, sex, 20 PCs; comparable evaluation setup). Within that cluster, PGS005083 has the highest reported full-model discrimination (C-index 0.75368) and the strongest reported per-SD effect size (OR 1.455, 95% CI 1.38–1.54), which is supportive of stronger PRS signal relative to its siblings. The two best-supported runners-up are PGS005077 (C-index 0.75358; OR 1.452) and PGS005076 (C-index 0.75325; OR 1.443), which are extremely close but slightly weaker on both metrics. Limitation: the key discrimination metric shown is full-model C-index (not explicitly PGS-only), so comparability across studies is imperfect and the apparent performance could be partly covariate-driven; several other direct-match heart-failure models exist (e.g., PGS001790 with a reported PRS-only R2=0.006981, and PGS005097 with AUROC 0.72) but they are harder to rank above the MVP CHF cluster from the visible evidence because their reported metrics are either not directly comparable or do not show stronger PRS-isolated signal than the selected model’s strong OR evidence.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to hip osteoarthritis by trait_efo/trait_reported, so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS002763 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Hip osteoarthritis” (good endpoint fidelity to the target) and it reports a comparatively strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46), which the provided domain guidance treats as meaningful PRS-quality evidence when AUC/R2 are missing. It also uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with a large variant set, consistent with stronger structural properties for polygenic traits.

Runners-up: PGS002728 is also explicitly “Hip osteoarthritis” but uses a proxy endpoint (“Total hip replacement”) and only provides a full-model AUROC (0.66 with age/sex), which domain guidance warns is not a substitute for PRS-only metrics; still, it is disease-focused and has clear reported discrimination. PGS004882 has a relevant endpoint (“Incident hip osteoarthritis”) and reports an HR=1.4 (95% CI 1.38–1.42) plus a C-index=0.6, but it appears in a broader incidence-framework context and lacks PRS-only metrics, making it harder to compare cleanly.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because most candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, several rely on non-identical endpoints (time-to-event, incident-only, or hip replacement), and covariates are unknown for some (e.g., PGS004478/PGS004548), leaving meaningful residual uncertainty despite multiple direct-match options.

Direct-match candidates for Hodgkin’s lymphoma are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 all have trait_efo=Hodgkins lymphoma and phenotyping_reported=Hodgkin’s disease). Among these, PGS000639 (P+T; 20 variants) has the strongest reported discrimination in the same evaluation setting (full-model AUROC 0.62; Nagelkerke R² 0.0276; OR per SD 1.476 [1.154–1.889]) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), making it the best-supported direct match in this visible list. Runners-up are PGS000638 (GWAS hits; 16 variants) with slightly lower AUROC (0.601) and OR (1.377) but otherwise identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry context, and PGS000637 (PRS-CS; genome-wide) which is endpoint-aligned but shows weaker reported performance here (AUROC 0.574; OR 1.3). Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because all Hodgkin-aligned options come from the same PRSweb publication family with small validation size (n=775) and only full-model metrics (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), limiting confidence in cross-model comparability and in how much of AUROC is PRS-driven versus covariate-driven.

Direct-match hypertension candidates are present (e.g., PGS004236/PGS004234/PGS001320/PGS002047/PGS001838/PGS000706/PGS004934, etc.). PGS004236 is best supported in the visible list because it is explicitly hypertension (trait_efo=hypertension; phenotyping_reported=prevalent hypertension) and comes from a disease-focused hypertension PRS paper (Nat Commun: “A multi-ethnic polygenic risk score is associated with hypertension prevalence and progression throughout adulthood.”) with multi-ethnic evaluation and a strong reported effect size (OR=2.1) plus a reasonably high full-model AUROC (0.764) using standard demographic/PC-style covariates plus BMI/smoking/site/race-ethnic background (not a heavy biomarker/family-history package per the provided domain guidance). Runner-up PGS004234 is from the same study family with the same endpoint and similar AUROC (0.763) but lacks the explicit OR evidence shown for PGS004236, leaving it slightly less supported. Third, PGS001320 is an exact hypertension endpoint with explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.629 and PGS-only R2=0.06493; incremental AUROC=0.04424) but it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”), which the domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; thus it ranks behind the Nat Commun hypertension-specific models. Main limitation: multiple strong direct-match hypertension models exist with partially non-comparable metrics (many report only full-model AUROC or partial correlation), and the chosen best model’s AUROC is full-model (not PRS-only), so confidence is not high despite strong endpoint alignment and effect-size support.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (hyperthyroidism), either as explicit hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis endpoints (PGS001042/PGS001043/PGS001815/PGS002023) or as Graves’ disease (PGS005264/PGS005265/PGS005266), which the provided domain knowledge explicitly treats as the dominant autoimmune form of clinical hyperthyroidism and therefore a strong direct match.

Best pick (PGS005265): Among the Graves’ disease models, PGS005265 has the strongest visible PRS-discrimination signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.625...) and the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.6652) within that Graves’ cluster, with multi-cohort development listed (many biobanks) and multi-ancestry evaluation noted (MAE 100%). This combination (dominant-subtype endpoint + stronger effect size within a coherent disease-focused family) is the most supportive package in the visible set.

Runners-up: (1) PGS005266 is a near-clone Graves’ disease PRSCS model from the same study family with slightly weaker effect size (OR 1.543...) and slightly lower AUROC (0.6637), making it the closest alternative. (2) PGS001043 is the strongest of the explicit hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis-labeled UKB framework scores by endpoint wording alignment (hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis) and slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.7137 vs 0.7130 for PGS001042), with explicit PGS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC 0.6323; PGS R2 0.0216) under basic covariates.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: The Graves’ disease candidates report only full-model AUROC and effect sizes (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability; meanwhile the hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis candidates come from identified pan-trait/portability-style UKB framework papers (a negative signal per domain knowledge) despite having explicit PGS-only metrics. This creates a meaningful evidence tradeoff (endpoint/study archetype vs metric comparability), so the best choice is preferred but not unequivocally decisive from the visible metadata alone.

PGS004911 is best supported because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~374k), and is an MTAG-enhanced sibling from the same publication family where MTAG is explicitly described in the provided domain knowledge as a legitimate power-boost and mildly preferred over the non-MTAG base. It also reports stronger overall validation metrics than its sibling PGS004910 (full-model AUROC 0.80 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; higher HR/OR), though these appear to be full-model/adjusted metrics rather than clearly PRS-only, which limits certainty. Runner-up PGS004910 is the closest comparable alternative (same paper, same endpoint/covariates, PRS-CS, similar variant count) but with weaker reported metrics. Third is PGS000739: direct HCM endpoint and large validation sample, but its reported AUROC (0.821) is explicitly full-model and includes multiple clinical risk-factor covariates plus rare-variant carrier status, making the discrimination less PRS-comparable per the domain guidance. Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=hypothyroidism). PGS005218 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused for hypothyroidism (publication: “Genome-wide association study and polygenic risk prediction of hypothyroidism”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,110,091 variants), and has the strongest visible discrimination evidence in the list (full-model AUROC=0.859 with a large validation sample n=441,692). Runners-up: (1) PGS004935 is a direct hypothyroidism endpoint with cleaner comparability than biomarker-adjusted models (covariates unknown rather than explicitly biomarker-heavy) and reports AUROC=0.70 plus OR=1.5 (CI 1.41–1.6), supporting meaningful PRS signal, though with smaller validation (n=8,417). (2) PGS002766 is also a direct hypothyroidism endpoint with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates) and reports OR=1.47 (CI 1.43–1.52) in EUR evaluation (n=39,444), but lacks AUC/R2. Other candidates are penalized for endpoint mismatch (therapy-induced hypothyroidism: PGS000759/PGS000761/PGS000820), framework/portability context (e.g., pan-trait UKB snpnet: PGS000965/PGS001181; UKB portability: PGS001816/PGS002024), very weak incremental R2 (several P+T models), or unclear comparability/limited metrics.
