All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (trait_efo includes osteoarthritis, knee), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS002729 is preferred because it is explicitly knee osteoarthritis with a clinical osteoarthritis phenotype and comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort development context (multiple OA-relevant cohorts listed), with an external validation AUROC reported (0.66 in Europeans), albeit as a full-model metric with covariates (age, sex, BMI) and without PGS-only AUROC/R2—so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared. Runner-up PGS002767 is also an exact knee osteoarthritis endpoint and reports a per-SD OR=1.35 (moderate discriminative signal) in a large European evaluation (n=39,444), but lacks AUROC/R2 and has no listed training cohorts, limiting comparability. Second runner-up PGS004549 targets the same gonarthrosis endpoint and uses an ensemble/metaPRS-style method (RFDiseasemetaPRS; structurally favorable) with OR=1.3667, but covariates are unknown and performance metrics are otherwise sparse, lowering confidence. PGS001192 is penalized as a pan-trait UKB framework score ("across 813 traits") with weak PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.557; PGS R2=0.0068) despite having detailed reporting; PGS002749 is a treatment/procedure proxy (total knee replacement) rather than generic KOA; PGS004479 is similar to PGS004549 but with slightly weaker OR; PGS004883 is incident-only and appears packaged for incidence estimation with small training n (404) and only a modest full-model C-index (0.6), making it less supported for generic KOA risk. Overall confidence is moderate because the best candidate’s key metric is full-model (not PGS-only) and several alternatives have only effect sizes without directly comparable discrimination metrics.

All 5 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS000054 and PGS000053 are the most endpoint-faithful: both target familial late-onset Alzheimer’s disease (LOAD) with basic covariates (age, sex) and report per-SD odds ratios, which domain guidance treats as meaningful PRS discrimination evidence when AUC/R2 are absent. Between them, PGS000054 has a materially stronger reported OR per SD (1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR 1.29, 1.21–1.37), making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the visible evidence, despite being evaluated in AMR/Hispanic/Latin American rather than EUR. As runners-up, PGS000053 remains strong due to the same study family, same endpoint framing, and EUR evaluation (but weaker OR). PGS000334 is the next best-supported because it has a direct LOAD endpoint and reports an R²-type metric (variance explained 0.191), but this value is potentially non-comparable/suspect per the provided domain guidance (high R² with C+T and unknown covariates), lowering confidence. Overall confidence is moderate because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R², covariates are unknown for several models, and one candidate (PGS002289) has a phenotyping_reported field that appears misaligned with disease diagnosis (cognition/age interaction), while PGS004918 reports only full-model AUROC (0.731) on a very small evaluation sample (n=136), which is not a PRS-only metric and is weak for cross-model ranking.

All ranked candidates are direct matches to the target trait (lung cancer) by trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS004860 is best supported in the visible list because it has a direct incident lung cancer endpoint, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2; 1,143,554 variants), and reports strong discrimination in its selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.893 with CI 0.887–0.898) plus an effect size (OR 1.33). The main limitation is that the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates (age/sex/BMI/smoking/PCs), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated from the metadata.

Runners-up: PGS000078 and PGS000789 are both direct incident lung cancer models in very large European validation (n=392,539) with consistent effect-size evidence (HR ~1.16–1.17) and the same covariate structure; they are strong and mutually corroborating but are based on genome-wide significant hits (109 variants) rather than genome-wide shrinkage, and their reported high full-model AUROC (0.846) is similarly not PRS-only. Other direct-match candidates are either endpoint-restricted (e.g., early-onset, never-smokers), broader composite endpoints (lung and bronchus), have weaker reported discrimination (e.g., PRSweb AUROCs ~0.52–0.54), or have missing/unknown performance details that prevent stronger support than the top three.

All listed candidates are direct matches to lupus erythematosus via either systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or lupus erythematosus (localized and systemic). PGS000328 is preferred because it targets SLE with a clear lupus diagnosis phenotype (early-onset SLE) and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the disease-focused, non-packaged candidates (full-model AUROC=0.83 in EUR; n=1,001). Key limitation: the AUROC is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided) and the phenotype is restricted to onset before age 20, so general SLE/lupus risk portability is uncertain. Runners-up: PGS000754 is a disease-focused SLE score using a genome-wide shrinkage method (lassosum) with very large variant count (293,684) and large validation (n=7,733), but its reported full-model AUROC is lower (0.65) and still not PRS-only. PGS000196 is also disease-focused SLE with moderate full-model AUROC (0.79) but has a smaller variant set (55) and a more context-specific phenotype (‘SLE diagnosis in patient with arthritis’) with smaller validation (n=245). Other candidates were deprioritized due to endpoint mismatch toward renal/nephritis/severity subphenotypes (PGS000771/PGS000772/PGS003755/PGS003756), phenotype-risk-score covariate packaging (PGS003960), broad/less disease-focused portability-framework origin with weak partial-r metrics (PGS001870/PGS002082), or unclear interaction-focused context (PGS004917). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target EFO concept (lymphoid leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305; plus several chronic lymphocytic leukemia models that are narrower than the target umbrella). PGS000077 is best supported as a direct match because its trait_efo is exactly lymphoid leukemia and its phenotyping_reported is an incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint with only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and it shows a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.45) in a large European evaluation sample (n=391,338). Runners-up: PGS000788 is also an exact lymphoid leukemia match with the same incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint and basic covariates, and shows a stronger reported HR (1.7) and slightly higher full-model AUROC/C-index; however, its method description indicates it uses inverse weights from PGS000077, creating uncertainty about correctness/standard directionality and making it less straightforward as a primary choice. PGS000645 is an exact lymphoid leukemia match with explicit AUROC (0.578) and OR per SD (1.358), but it is extremely sparse (6 variants) and has a much smaller validation sample (n=957), limiting confidence. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because across the direct-match set, most reported discrimination is full-model (not clearly PRS-only), and there is meaningful ambiguity between closely related lymphoid/lymphocytic/chronic lymphocytic endpoints and between PGS000077 vs the inverse-weight derivative PGS000788.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS004606 is best supported because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD genetics study (Nat Genet; IAMDGC training cohort), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and provides supportive performance/effect evidence (full-model AUROC=0.71 with basic covariates; OR per SD=1.76, which is strong). Remaining limitation: the AUROC shown is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), so comparability across models is imperfect and lowers confidence.

Runner-up PGS004952 is also disease-focused and endpoint-specific (late age-related macular degeneration), but its reported AUROC appears internally inconsistent (classification_metrics AUROC listed as 84.2 vs performance_metrics.full_model_auc=0.842) and it has a much smaller validation sample (n=1,232), making the performance evidence less reliable from the visible metadata despite strong apparent discrimination.

Runner-up PGS004607 is from the same 2024 Nat Genet study family and has the same endpoint/covariates structure, but shows weaker visible performance/effect evidence than PGS004606 (full-model AUROC=0.65; OR=1.48). The remaining candidates (PGS001013, PGS001834, PGS002041) are from pan-trait/portability UKB framework papers with weaker or non-comparable metrics (e.g., partial-r ~0.016–0.018 or small PGS-only AUROC ~0.553), and PGS002269 has a phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness biomarker rather than direct AMD diagnosis), so they are less supported as primary direct-match choices.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma endpoints). PGS000813 is best supported in the visible list because it has strong endpoint alignment (familial cutaneous melanoma in non-carriers of CDKN2A mutation; still melanoma), and it reports comparatively strong discrimination/effect evidence (full_model AUROC 0.77 with OR per SD 2.12 and OR top 10% vs middle 20% 5.7), with EUR evaluation. Main limitation: the endpoint is a restricted familial/non-CDKN2A subgroup rather than a general-population melanoma endpoint, which may reduce generalizability versus population-based incident melanoma models.

Runner-up 1 PGS000743: direct melanoma endpoint with high reported full_model AUROC (0.74, EUR), but the covariate set includes many traditional melanoma risk factors (e.g., pigmentation traits, nevi, family history, sun exposure), making the full-model AUROC likely covariate-inflated and less PRS-comparable.

Runner-up 2 PGS002247: direct-match incident invasive melanoma with clean/basic covariates (age, sex) and solid full_model AUROC (0.691) plus reported R2 (0.072), but its discrimination is lower than PGS000813 and it lacks the very strong per-SD effect size evidence shown for PGS000813 in the visible metadata.

All 6 listed candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo (multiple myeloma / plasma cell myeloma), but one (PGS003450) has an explicit endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (chronic lymphocytic leukemia), which materially weakens its direct-match support despite the trait label. Among the remaining coherent multiple-myeloma endpoints, PGS002281 has the strongest visible discrimination evidence with a relatively high full-model AUROC (0.644; European validation) and a strong stratification effect (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles), with covariates limited to basic demographics/region. PGS002306 reports an even higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but has a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and unknown covariates, making its performance less interpretable/comparable; it is therefore the top runner-up. For the second runner-up, PGS000653 is preferred over its close sibling PGS000654 because it shows slightly higher AUROC (0.577 vs 0.576), higher pseudo-R² (0.0145 vs 0.0137), and slightly stronger per-SD OR (1.327 vs 1.316) under the same basic covariate set and endpoint family. Overall confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so ranking relies on full-model metrics and effect sizes, which are less directly comparable across studies.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002726 is best supported because it is disease-focused (IMSGC), endpoint-aligned (Multiple sclerosis), and reports the strongest visible discrimination among the set via a European validation AUROC=0.80 (PPM014750) plus a large risk-gradient metric (OR top 10% vs median=15.0). Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with covariates listed as 'Unknown', and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, reducing comparability across candidates. Runner-up PGS000809 is also disease-focused with clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and reports full-model AUROC=0.765 and R²=0.069, but likewise lacks PRS-only metrics and has lower AUROC than PGS002726. Third-ranked PGS002038 (LDpred2, genome-wide) has strong methodological/structural properties and a slightly higher partial-r (0.0396) than its sibling PGS001831, but it lacks AUROC/R² and comes from a portability-style UKB-derived study family, making it less directly supported than the disease-focused MS-specific publications above.

Direct-match myocardial infarction candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction). PGS005039 is best supported within the visible list because it is a direct MI endpoint (PheCode 411.2; phenotyping_reported: Myocardial infarction) and shows the strongest combined discriminative evidence among the MI-labeled set: highest reported full-model C-index (~0.7848) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), which domain guidance treats as strong PRS signal (OR≥1.5). The top runners-up are PGS005035 (direct MI; similarly strong C-index ~0.7834 and OR=1.541) and PGS005045 (direct MI; C-index ~0.7839 and OR=1.554). Confidence is Moderate because these MVP-derived MI models are near-clones with very similar reported C-index values and broadly similar design/metadata, and the reported discrimination is full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), limiting how decisively performance can separate them.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = "Nasal Cavity Polyp"; phenotyping_reported = ICD10 J33 "Nasal polyp"), come from the same publication (Commun Biol, 2024-03-18), same training cohort (UKB), same EUR-only DEV/EVAL ancestry distribution, same variant count (1,059,939), and same validation sample size (n=56,192). With endpoint fidelity and transportability effectively tied, the main differentiator in the visible evidence is effect size: PGS004535 reports a stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.600668) than PGS004465 (OR=1.3496), which domain guidance treats as stronger discriminative signal when AUC/R2 are missing. However, both models lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (AUC/R2 all null) and have covariates listed as "Unknown", limiting comparability and preventing a high-confidence selection; hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL with moderate confidence.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = nicotine dependence; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Tobacco use disorder) and come from the same UKB portability publication with similar training (UKB; n=391,124), validation size (n=19,400), and basic covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs). With endpoint fidelity and study context essentially tied, the main differentiator is the available PRS-comparable performance metric: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), and it also uses a genome-wide shrinkage-style method (LDpred2) with substantially more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is supportive structurally. Confidence is not High because both models are from the same portability framework paper (a known limitation for external generalization per the provided domain knowledge) and neither reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, leaving only partial-r for quantitative comparison.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (nodular goiter) via either explicit benign nodular goiter endpoints (PGS005261/PGS005262/PGS005263) or closely aligned multinodular/nontoxic goiter endpoints (PGS001814/PGS002022); two additional models (PGS005273/PGS005274) include benign nodular goiter in a case-control contrast but are not pure nodular-goiter risk scores. PGS005262 is best supported because it is explicitly for benign nodular goiter (phenotyping_reported aligns despite minor spelling noise), comes from a disease-focused multi-biobank study family, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count, and has the strongest reported discrimination among the benign nodular goiter models (full-model AUROC 0.5933) plus moderate per-SD effect size evidence (OR ~1.41). The main limitation is that the only reported AUROC appears to be full-model (covariates are listed as Unknown), so PRS-only performance comparability is unclear; this keeps the overall decision at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL. For runners-up, PGS005273 and PGS005274 have the highest AUROCs in the visible list (0.617 and 0.613) and strong per-SD ORs (~1.55 and ~1.49), but their endpoint is thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter (a contrast phenotype rather than nodular goiter status), making them less endpoint-faithful for nodular goiter risk than PGS005262.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo=obesity and/or obesity-coded endpoints. PGS005235 is best supported on endpoint fidelity and study design coherence: although trait_reported is broader (“Adiposity”), phenotyping_reported is an explicit obesity diagnosis endpoint (phecode: 278.1), and it uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with large genome-wide coverage (709,828 variants) and multi-cohort training sources (EGG, GIANT, UKB), which is structurally favorable versus UKB-only framework/portability scores. However, confidence is limited because most candidates (including PGS005235) lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²), leaving only effect sizes (OR) without clear per-SD definition/comparability across studies.

Runners-up: (1) PGS004447 is a direct ICD10 E66 obesity endpoint with LDpred2 and very large variant count (1,059,939) and UKB training; it has an OR effect size reported, but covariates are unknown and it is single-cohort. (2) PGS002033 is a direct-match obesity/overweight phenotype from a known portability framework; despite the framework penalty, it provides a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0789 with CI) and uses LDpred2 with very large variant count (846,292), making it more evidentially grounded than other metric-sparse candidates. PGS001298 is deprioritized despite having explicit AUROC/R² because it is from a pan-trait sparse framework (“813 traits”) and uses a time-to-event obesity definition, both of which are negative signals in the provided domain guidance.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the pool has heterogeneous endpoint definitions (generic osteoporosis vs M81 without pathological fracture vs time-to-event) and many models lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) or have unknown covariates, limiting a clearly high-quality pick.

PGS002768 is preferred because it is a direct osteoporosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis) and provides an interpretable PRS effect size (OR per SD = 1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates) and EUR-only evaluation, giving the strongest standalone PRS signal among candidates with explicit effect-size evidence.

Runner-up PGS004565 is also a direct osteoporosis endpoint and reports a slightly higher OR (1.328222), but its covariates are listed as Unknown and it comes from a risk-factor integration publication family, making comparability and PRS-isolation less clear from the visible metadata.

Runner-up PGS001273 is a direct osteoporosis endpoint with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.5685; PGS R2 0.00688) and basic covariates; however it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly, and its PRS-only performance is modest. Overall, missing/heterogeneous performance reporting across the set prevents a high-confidence single best choice.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred because its endpoint is the generic disease label (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: "Otosclerosis") rather than a time-to-event formulation, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (570,308 variants), which is structurally favorable versus the sparse snpnet model. However, the evidence is limited because PGS002046 lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R² in the provided metrics (only partial correlation is reported), while PGS001255 reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.6319) and PGS-only R² (0.01341) plus full-model AUROC (0.6532) on European validation. Both models come from UK Biobank framework-style publications ("across 813 traits" and "Portability of 245 polygenic scores"), which reduces confidence that either is clearly best for real-world use, hence a sub-optimal direct-match outcome.

Direct-match candidates are present, including multiple models whose trait_efo is exactly the target (ovarian neoplasm) and phenotyping_reported is “Malignant neoplasm of ovary” (PGS000544–PGS000564). Among these exact-endpoint matches, PGS000549 has the strongest visible discrimination (full_model AUROC 0.567 with EUR evaluation) and strong supporting effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.263, 95% CI 1.15–1.387) with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), making it the best-supported direct match in the provided list. The two closest runners-up are PGS000550 (very similar endpoint/covariates, slightly higher AUROC 0.568 and slightly higher OR 1.286) and PGS000551 (AUROC 0.558, OR 1.234), all from the same PRSweb publication family with comparable design.

Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY) because the key performance evidence available for these exact-label models is primarily full-model AUROC (not explicitly PRS-only), and several near-clone candidates have very similar endpoints and metrics, leaving residual uncertainty about which would be best under a PRS-only comparison. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 11 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma, with one dominant-subtype option (PGS002264: pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) also plausibly aligned. However, across the set, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are not reported; most AUC values shown are full-model AUROC and are not directly comparable across differing covariate sets, which limits certainty.

PGS000083 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), is evaluated in Europeans, and provides comparatively strong effect-size evidence (HR per SD 1.49 with CI) alongside a reported AUROC/C-index (~0.745/0.742) in a very large validation sample (n=391,491). While its covariates include family history and smoking/BMI (which can inflate full-model discrimination and reduce PRS-only interpretability), the combination of coherent phenotype definition plus strong per-SD effect size makes it the most defensible direct-match pick from the visible metadata.

Runners-up: PGS000794 is essentially the same 22-variant score family with very similar endpoint (incident pancreatic cancer), similar effect size (HR 1.49) and similar AUROC/C-index (~0.745/0.743) in the same large validation size, but it is explicitly described as using inverse variant weights relative to PGS000083, creating ambiguity about whether it is a straightforward PRS improvement or a reparameterization; this prevents it from clearly outranking PGS000083. PGS000663 remains a strong alternative due to direct phenotype alignment and an OR per SD of 1.44 with AUROC 0.67, but its evaluation sample is much smaller (n=956) and includes a broader covariate set (including diabetic status and anthropometrics), further limiting comparability.

Key limitation driving the DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL outcome: the evidence provided does not include PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R2) for any candidate, and several reported AUROCs are likely covariate-influenced, so the ranking relies heavily on endpoint fidelity and effect sizes rather than clean, comparable PRS performance.

All 11 listed candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease), but several are progression/incident-only or otherwise endpoint-shifted (e.g., cognitive/motor decline, incident PD, PD dementia), which weakens a single clearly dominant choice for generic Parkinson disease risk.

PGS000903 is best supported because it has a direct PD endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Parkinson's disease), comes from a large disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication family (Lancet Neurol 2021), uses a more polygenic construction than GWAS-hits-only siblings (C+T with 1,805 variants), and is the only candidate here with an explicit PRS-comparable metric (reported R²=0.054) plus a strong risk-gradient effect size (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25). Main limitation: the visible AUROC is full-model (0.692) rather than PGS-only, and covariate-adjusted metrics are not directly comparable across candidates.

Runner-up PGS000902 is from the same strong Lancet Neurol 2021 family with the same direct PD endpoint and very large training context, but it is a GWAS-hits score (90 variants) and provides only full-model AUROC (0.651) with no PRS-only R²/effect-size gradient shown here.

Runner-up PGS003763 has good endpoint fidelity for risk (phenotyping_reported: Incident Parkinson Disease) and a very large validation sample (n=314,998) with a clear HR separation (1.72 high vs low tertile), but it is incident-only (not generic case-control PD) and lacks PRS-only discrimination metrics, making it harder to prefer over the Lancet Neurol disease-meta-analysis scores.

All 4 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level for the target (peripheral vascular disease), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and study archetype. PGS005217 is best supported because it is disease-focused on peripheral artery disease with an explicit incident PAD endpoint, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (1,296,292), has large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=304,294 across multiple ancestries), and reports a strong PRS-associated effect size (HR=1.66 per SD). Main limitation: its trait is PAD (a major subtype within peripheral vascular disease) rather than the broader/unspecified PVD label, and the only AUC-like metric shown is a full-model C-index (0.731), not a PGS-only metric.

Runners-up: PGS002055 and PGS001843 match the target label exactly (PVD unspecified; EFO peripheral vascular disease) but come from a UKB portability framework paper rather than a disease-focused PAD study, and their only PRS-comparable evidence is small partial correlations (0.0175 and 0.0151, respectively). Between them, PGS002055 is preferred over PGS001843 due to the stronger partial-r and substantially larger variant count (599,514 vs 242) within the same publication family and evaluation context. PGS005158 is ranked below these runners-up because its phenotype is restricted to PAD in type 2 diabetes with heavy clinical covariate adjustment and only a modest HR (1.13), making it less comparable for generic PVD risk despite being PAD-aligned.

All three candidates are direct-match at the ontology level (trait_efo=preeclampsia). By endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported), PGS003586 and PGS003587 are most coherent for preeclampsia because both use a pre-eclampsia/eclampsia phenotype, whereas PGS004593 has an internal mismatch (trait_reported=Preeclampsia but phenotyping_reported=Gestational hypertension), which weakens endpoint alignment per the provided domain guidance. Among the two Nat Med sibling models (same publication family, same method PRS-CS, similar variant counts, same EUR evaluation), PGS003586 has stronger effect-size evidence (OR 1.31 [1.24–1.38]) than PGS003587 (OR 1.20 [1.14–1.26]), making it the best-supported direct-match choice. Confidence is not High because none of the candidates report PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only effect sizes), and PGS004593’s phenotype/label inconsistency introduces ambiguity in the overall evidence pool.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches to the target trait (prostate cancer / prostate carcinoma) based on trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS004155 is best supported in the visible list because it targets the direct disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Prostate cancer"), uses an explicitly PRS-focused evaluation setting with no added covariates (covariates: "0"), is evaluated on a large European validation sample (n=171,474), and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the comparable no-covariate models from the same benchmarking family (full_model_auc=0.7049; full_model_r2=0.1280). The two runners-up are close siblings from the same study with the same endpoint and covariate setting and nearly identical validation context: PGS004139 (SBayesR-auto; full_model_auc=0.7003; full_model_r2=0.1213) and PGS004042 (LDpred2.CV; full_model_auc=0.6994; full_model_r2=0.1202). Confidence is Moderate because many other direct-match models exist in the provided list with different endpoints (e.g., aggressive/lethal/fatal, age-of-onset hazard scores, 5-year incident risk packaging) and heterogeneous covariate designs, making cross-study metric comparability imperfect; additionally, the reported AUC/R2 here are labeled as full-model metrics (even though covariates are 0), and no explicit PGS-only AUROC is provided for most candidates.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (psoriasis) are present (multiple models with trait_efo=psoriasis and phenotyping_reported indicating psoriasis endpoints). PGS001312 is the best-supported direct match because it has exact endpoint alignment (trait_efo=psoriasis; phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis) and provides PRS-comparable performance metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.69158) and PGS-only R² (0.05226), plus full-model AUROC (0.69754) with standard/basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). The two strongest runners-up from the same candidate list are PGS001871 and PGS002083: both are exact psoriasis endpoints (phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis) from the UKB portability study with multi-ancestry evaluation and report comparable PRS-only-style metrics (partial correlation ~0.063), but they lack explicit AUROC/R² in the provided record, making them less directly comparable than PGS001312. Confidence is Moderate because several other direct-match psoriasis models exist (including time-to-event and severity-focused endpoints, and models with missing/heterogeneous metrics), and the evidence does not include a clearly superior disease-focused multi-cohort psoriasis-risk PRS with stronger PRS-only discrimination than PGS001312.

Direct-match candidates present: PGS000342 (Psoriatic arthritis) and PGS001287 (Psoriatic arthropathy; trait_efo=psoriatic arthritis). Both are phenotype-aligned to the target.
